text:
BERT4Rec already includes final-item training: §3.6 describes random masked-item reconstruction plus examples masking only the last item, with appended-mask inference. The official generator mixes `dupe_factor` random-mask copies and one last-only copy per sequence window, then shuffles them. With the supplied ML-1M script’s `dupe_factor=10`, dedicated last-only examples constitute 1/11 ≈ 9.1%; random copies can also select the final position. This is interleaved training, despite the paper’s fine-tuning analogy. [Paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1904.06690), [generator](https://github.com/FeiSun/BERT4Rec/blob/master/gen_data_fin.py), [script](https://github.com/FeiSun/BERT4Rec/blob/master/run_ml-1m.sh).

Normalization matters: Equation 8 averages negative log-likelihood over masked targets within a sequence. Official `run.py` instead sums weighted target cross-entropies across the minibatch and divides by total target weight plus `1e-5`; real targets have weight 1, padded target slots 0. Consequently, a random-mask example with k targets contributes k target terms, versus one for a last-only example. For equal k, the dedicated last-only contribution is approximately 1/(10k+1), rather than 1/11 of target weight. [Loss implementation](https://github.com/FeiSun/BERT4Rec/blob/master/run.py).

The original paper reports no dedicated sweep of last-only example frequency or removal ablation. Related experiments compare single-random-mask training with ordinary Cloze training (§4.4, Table 3) and sweep overall masking proportion ρ=0.1–0.9 (§4.6, Figure 4); neither isolates final-item allocation. Increasing that allocation therefore reweights an existing mechanism. Host-baseline mixture, normalization, and proposed allocation must be documented separately from supplied host code, which was not included here. [Paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1904.06690).
